paragraphs.text: Beast is a catch-all creature type used for large, monstrous, animal-like creatures. The first creature to bear the type was Beasts of Bogardan in Legends but in pluralized form. Clockwork Beast from Alpha and Guardian Beast from Arabian Nights were later issued errata to become beast, but it wasn't until Tempest that the Beast subtype attained widespread usage and was also printed as such. Later, in the Odyssey and Onslaught blocks , "beast" became a common subtype with considerable inter-card support.

In the Grand Creature Type Update the creature types Carnivore ( Tooth and Claw ), Lurker ( Lurker ), Villain ( Spinal Villain ) and Frostbeast ( Kjeldoran Frostbeast ) were changed into Beast. On the other hand Glowing Anemone was changed from Beast to Anemone , while later reverting to Beast and gaining the added Jellyfish type. Warthog briefly merged with Beast ( Giant Warthog ) before becoming Boar .

Alacrian quickbeasts are huge winged creatures which, fueled by a diet of aether , are capable of startlingly quick, sustained movement and propelling themselves and their riders at high speeds across varied terrain for days at a time between feedings. They are intelligent creatures, ancient and valued by the riders who they choose to partner with. Riders must pass through extensive schooling and training before they can mount a Quickbeast, and even then, only with the consent of the beast.
Each district of Alacria's city has a mascot called a "soul" that is embodied in a quickbeast with a soul-linked human counterpart. These bonds can be forged, reforged, and discovered in new pairs.

Duskmourn's beasts, known as " Beasties " ( 16 cards ), are intelligent animals who befriend and protect Survivors. Originally the plane's former pets that transformed during Valgavoth 's Ascension, they are small when young, and then they spin silk cocoons and emerge as large, shaggy, furred adults. They generally have more than four limbs, claws, horns, and fangs, and wear masks. Beasties don't have mouths that necessarily allow for comprehensible speech, but they're fully intelligent, and they can understand what's said to them. Though they are predators, they don't eat intelligent creatures.

The face beneath a beastie's mask is their most guarded secret. Beasties live in constant fear of their human companions seeing their real faces, which are visages of dried flesh tethered to exposed skulls. Beasties know these faces are terrifying, hideous mockeries of living flesh. If a human does ever catch a glimpse of a beastie's real face, the beastie will abandon them or even grow enraged and attack, driven in anger to kill anyone who knows its true appearance.

Beasties originally lived in one large pack, presenting an easy target for the House's monsters. When their leader, Spindlewight, rescued two children, the beasties found their purpose in protecting the House's survivors, who they refer to as "keep-alives." These first two survivors began painting the mural that the beasties keep in the attic and established the convention of wearing and never removing masks. After one of Spindlewight's keep-alives saw his maskless face, they fled into the house, causing him to renounce his leadership and the fracturing of the beasties into multiple packs. The mural was kept as neutral ground between the factions.

Above all, beasties want to be loved and appreciated. They find smiles to be the greatest gifts from their companions, and crying to be unbearably painful. They have a particular fondness for children, possibly because children are the most likely to accept them. Beasties are fiercely loyal to their companions, and won't hesitate to attack anyone who threatens their new friend.

Herbivorous Beasts form one of the dominant clades of Ikoria and are mainly associated with the lush forests of Zagoth . Identifiable by their woolly fur, horns or antlers, and stumpy or cloven feet, most of them resemble large herbivores — elk , rhinos , camels , boars , and the like — but it is dangerous to conclude that they are at all docile. Even smaller beast monsters are territorial and irascible, liable to stampede or trample when they are alarmed or threatened. While most are large and lumbering, there are also many smaller, graceful beasts that more closely resemble horses or antelopes .
